conf.description: cyberark-pam vault-audit / syslog-leef: hand-built LEEF envelope parser (the stock cyberarkpas integration ingests CEF/JSON only, not LEEF). CyberArk does not publicly document the LEEF.xsl body-attribute key names, so only the 5 header-documented fields are mapped to ECS; every tab-separated extension attribute is preserved verbatim in a generic namespaced bucket rather than guessing at Issuer/Safe/File/Station equivalents.

conf.comment: cyberark-pam / vault-audit / syslog-leef. No Elastic integration parses LEEF for this technology. The work order's own framing: CyberArk does NOT publicly document the LEEF.xsl body-attribute names (Issuer/Safe/File/Station etc.) - only the LEEF header (Version/Vendor/Product/ProductVersion/MessageID-as-EventID) and the LEEF-standard devTime attribute are sourceable from vendor/DSM docs, so the field table is intentionally limited to those 5, and this pipeline does not invent the rest. Real structural parsing done here: split the LEEF:Version|Cyber-Ark|Vault|<ver>|<MessageID>| header into ECS, then tab-split the extension into a generic cyberark_pam.leef.attrs.<key> bucket (nested JS in code, not restricted eval/rename path syntax) so a real captured sample's attributes are preserved and queryable once one exists. devTime is best-effort promoted to _time - its exact format string is unconfirmed per the work order. Direct route, no guard hop.
